organization.name: The Civic Order
organization.entry:
The Civic Order is Fogport's authoritarian municipal government, created after the Catastrophe destroyed the old royal government. The royal family vanished, the palace was ruined, and Vauntin Quell seized control of the city.

He did not declare himself king. Instead, he declared himself Vauntin Quell, First Citizen of the Civic Order. The title sounds humble and democratic. It is neither.

The Civic Order claims that the monarchy failed Fogport and that the city requires practical administration rather than hereditary ceremony. Vauntin insists he accepted leadership only because somebody had to keep Fogport alive. He has now been First Citizen for forty-three years.

The Hall of Civic Order

The government occupies the immense Hall of Civic Order at the head of the Grand Promenade. Once a royal administrative annex, it now contains offices, bridges, lifts, archives, furnaces, waiting rooms, interrogation chambers, and clerical dormitories. Its foundations supposedly descend farther underground than the building rises into the fog.

The Hall contains hundreds of brass service windows, forty-seven entrances, enormous portraits of Vauntin, a constantly corrected map of Fogport, three towering guillotines, and the Submerged Civic Holding Facility.

The Civic Seven

Vauntin initially created a thirty-six-seat senate-like Civic Assembly. After members began asking dangerous questions, resigning, disappearing, or suffering sudden illnesses, it was reduced to seven members called the Civic Seven.

They meet in the former Royal Opera Theater, a vast domed hall originally designed to seat 556 senators. The theater was built for royal political spectacles, not practical governance. Its enormous balconies, marble staircases, gilded boxes, acoustic vaults, and private ministerial corridors remain almost entirely unused.

The seven senators sit scattered across the immense chamber. One sits beneath the dome. One occupies the royal box. Two sit near the orchestra pit. The remaining three are separated by several hundred empty seats.

They communicate through brass speaking tubes, messenger boys, semaphore flags, and occasionally very loud shouting.

The arrangement is an enormous waste of space, money, heat, staff, and dignity. It also makes meaningful debate nearly impossible.

They do not legislate. They witness. Decrees are read aloud before them, and they confirm that every decision was made “in the civic interest.”

The chamber contains 556 seats. Seven are occupied. The remaining 549 are reserved for The Citizens Yet to Be Chosen.

The Civic Vigilance

The Civic Vigilance is the enforcement arm of the Civic Order: police, political intelligence service, licensing authority, public-order militia, and secret police. It suppresses sedition, labor unrest, unauthorized magic, public gatherings, criticism of Quell, and dangerous knowledge about the Catastrophe.

Its maxim is: The Guard watched the city. The Vigilance watches for it.

The Civic Bureaus

The Civic Order governs through more than fifty departments, each with its own seal, queue, tax, archive, and official authorized to say no.

  • The Chartered Duel Corps: licensed professional duelists who represent wealthy citizens in regulated challenges.
  • The Collegium Liaison Bureau: manages the government’s relationship with the Collegium of Lumen and licensed Lumeneers.
  • The Bureau of Lumen Extraction and Illumination: oversees fog harvesting, Lumen allotments, and public light.
  • The Bureau of Electric Illumination: regulates lightbulbs, filaments, wiring, meters, and unauthorized brightness.
  • The Office of Candle and Wick Preservation: maintains candle reserves for outages, funerals, séances, archives, and underground spaces.
  • The Bureau of Bellworks Production: oversees the economically vital Bellworks factories, foundries, clockworks, wireworks, engines, tram parts, and military machinery.
  • The Office of Industrial Celebrations: organizes factory anniversaries, engine unveilings, Foundry Days, labor parades, and public machinery demonstrations.
  • The First Citizen’s Reserve: Fogport’s central bank, controlling currency, state loans, aristocratic debt, factory investment, inheritance, foreign exchange, and bankruptcy.
  • The Bureau of Civic Credit and Moral Solvency: determines whether citizens are financially trustworthy and politically reliable.
  • The Bureau of Posts, Teeth, and Personal Correspondence: delivers letters, parcels, summonses, tooth powders, dentures, and official gum-health notices.
  • The Bureau of Food Importation and Foreign Provision: manages imported grain, meat, salt, coffee, sugar, preserved fish, and foreign delicacies.
  • The Bureau of Ale, Beer, and Wine Importation: imports, taxes, labels, and officially tests beverages Fogport cannot produce.
  • The Bureau of Bread Weight and Crust Integrity: inspects loaves and prosecutes concealed sawdust.
  • The Bureau of Public Hunger: maintains grain reserves, soup kitchens, famine registers, and a list of citizens likely to become troublesome if underfed.
  • The Department of Squalor Management: the only bureau assigned specifically to the Shambles. It has little money, little culture, three permanent officials, and one cracked cart.
  • The Office of Licensed Begging: issues colored badges and assigns approved beggars to street corners.
  • The Bureau of Brothel Linen Registration: registers sheets, towels, mattress ticking, and the frequency with which each is boiled.
  • The Bureau of Public Noise, Song, and Recorded Sound: regulates bells, whistles, street music, song publishing rights, wax cylinders, and patriotic choruses.
  • The Office of Civic Questions: fields public questions and classifies them as useful, repetitive, confused, already answered, or hostile to civic stability.
  • The Bureau of Fog Forecasting: predicts fog density, direction, toxicity, and fog of an argumentative nature.
  • The Bureau of Water, Bathing, and Drowning: regulates baths, swimming, canals, drowning prevention, drowning investigations, and approved ways to drown.
  • The Office of Royal Remnants, Succession, and Assassination: searches obsessively for surviving royals so Vauntin can have them killed.
  • The Bureau of Assassins and Miscellaneous Night Work: regulates assassination contracts, graveyards, night-soil collection, midnight deliveries, professional haunting, and other nocturnal activities.
  • The Bureau of Aerial Objects and Public Celebration: regulates kites, zeppelins, party orbs, blast gliders, balloons, and falling objects.
  • The Bureau of Industrial Engines: regulates engines of above-average size, including walking engines, fog pumps, bridge engines, and machines whose operators insist they are alive.
  • The Bureau of Juice Viscosity and Unusual Nighttime Activities: regulates thick drinks, syrups, moonlit duels, rooftop dining, private fireworks, and suspicious chanting.
  • The Office of Umbrella Registration: registers umbrellas by owner, diameter, color, ribs, and intended use.
  • The Bureau of Medical Celebration and Foulpractice Insurance: organizes medical festivities and insures against incorrect amputations, experimental treatment, accidental resurrection, and unauthorized organs.
  • The Bureau of Mob Calamities and Surprise Disappearances: explains riots, stampedes, mass vanishings, and inconvenient absences.
  • The Bureau of Printing Presses and Newspaper Review: regulates presses, newspapers, pamphlets, cartoons, and headlines that might cause panic.
  • The Office of Kindling and Domestic Flame: regulates firewood, coal scraps, braziers, stoves, and suspiciously dry sticks.
  • The Bureau of Trams and Conductors: operates the trams and employs Civic Transit Officers to enforce fares, seating, luggage rules, and tram-dueling restrictions.
  • The Bureau of Civic Childhood: operates Fogport’s one official school, the Municipal School of Civic Childhood, for children under thirty.
  • The Office of Parades and Approved Enthusiasm: organizes civic processions, industrial celebrations, medical festivals, executions, dueling exhibitions, and patriotic unveilings.

Additional Civic Bureaus

  • The Bureau of Lost Mud Disposal and Retrieval: handles mud that has been misplaced, stolen, abandoned, imported, or deposited in the wrong district. Citizens may file claims for lost mud by color, moisture, source, and intended use.
  • The Office of Whisper and Handkerchief Mediation: resolves disputes involving whispers, overheard remarks, coded gestures, sneezes, handkerchief colors, and allegedly threatening fabric.
  • The Bureau of Coal Dust Recovery: collects coal dust from factories, chimneys, clothing, lungs, monuments, and children’s eyelashes, then resells it to the Bellworks.
  • The Bureau of Fishermen and Fish: licenses fishermen, registers boats, classifies fish, regulates nets and bait, and determines how many fish may legally be called “a good catch.”
  • The Office of Gutter Placement and Civic Drainage: decides where gutters, downspouts, channels, spillways, and roof drains may be placed. It has authority over every puddle larger than a dinner plate.
  • The Bureau of Plumbing Mysteries: investigates pipes that knock, drains that whisper, faucets that produce brine, toilets that flush upward, and water that arrives before it has been ordered.
  • The Office of Artificial Limb Refitting and Enhancement: regulates prosthetic limbs, replacement joints, mechanical hands, reinforced legs, and unauthorized improvements. Limbs capable of crushing doors, outrunning trams, or concealing weapons require additional permits.
  • The Bureau of Shadow Analysis: studies shadows that do not match their owners, fall in the wrong direction, arrive before their bodies, or refuse to disappear at noon.
  • The Office of Dream Recovery and Investment: recovers lost, stolen, inherited, or misassigned dreams and accepts investments in dreams that may become inventions, political movements, commercial ventures, or religions.

The Drip Cages

The Submerged Civic Holding Facility is remarkably small. Prisoners are kept in narrow iron cages suspended beneath the Hall over a black reservoir. When lowered, their bodies hang in darkness while their heads remain barely above the water. They are reeled up for torture, questioning, medical inspection, public confession, or poetry performances.

The Civic Order calls them Suspended Civic Chambers. Citizens call them the Drip Cages. The Civic Order does not ask permission to torture; it submits the paperwork afterward.

The Guillotine Towers

The three enormous guillotines on the Hall are called The Past, The Present, and The Necessary Future. The Past is used for executions. The Present is used for demonstrations and warnings. The Necessary Future has never been used.

Every noon, one blade is dropped without a victim, producing a report heard across the Grand Promenade.

Efficiencies and Failures

The Civic Order keeps the trams running, maintains grain reserves, fights fires, repairs public lighting, regulates dangerous magic, identifies plague outbreaks, and makes foreign trade possible.

It also delays emergencies over jurisdiction, sends supplies according to obsolete maps, issues tax notices to the dead, declares living citizens deceased, collects the same tax under several names, hides mistakes beneath paperwork, and leaves the Shambles to rot.

The government knows where every citizen is supposed to be. It does not necessarily know where they actually are.

Vauntin Quell

The Civic Order reflects Vauntin perfectly: orderly but vain, practical but theatrical, obsessed with records, suspicious of anything that cannot be licensed, and incapable of admitting that Fogport might survive without him.

He does not want to be remembered as a king. He wants to be remembered as the man who made kings unnecessary.

That is why the Civic Order is the perfect name. It suggests that Fogport is not ruled by one man.

Everyone knows better.
